title: Adaptive Safety Constraints via Lagrangian Reward Augmentation for Inference-Time Alignment
summary: We propose integrating Lagrangian Reward Augmentation (LARA) with dynamic safety constraints to balance helpfulness and harmlessness during inference. LARA calibrates dual variables on a calibration set to adjust reward scores, ensuring safety constraints are satisfied while optimizing for helpfulness. We validate this approach on public safety benchmarks, comparing it to fixed-penalty and unconstrained baselines using AU-PRC and human evaluations.
gap: Existing inference-time alignment methods either ignore safety constraints or use manually tuned penalties, leading to suboptimal trade-offs between helpfulness and harmlessness. LARA provides a principled way to handle safety constraints without manual tuning, but its effectiveness under dynamic safety thresholds remains unexplored.
approach: We extend LARA by introducing adaptive safety constraints that adjust based on prompt complexity. The dual variable is recalibrated per prompt using a small calibration set, ensuring the augmented reward dynamically balances helpfulness and harmlessness. This is applied to Best-of-N reranking and token-level decoding.
evaluation: We compare against fixed-penalty BoN, unconstrained BoN, and Llama Guard baselines on HarmBench and StrongREJECT. Metrics include AU-PRC for safety, human preference for helpfulness, and attack success rates under jailbreaking. Ablations test calibration set size and constraint tightness.
